clue.text: Copied design of underwear chafing after two seconds

indicators.note: the chafing word is placed after the two seconds, so it follows them in the answer

parts.note: a bra is an item of women's underwear
S is the abbreviation for second; two of them give SS
chafing is rubbing

explanation.surface: Someone complains that their underwear started rubbing after just a couple of seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: A brass rubbing is made by rubbing paper laid over a church memorial brass, copying its design.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass rubbing is a reproduction of an engraved memorial plate, so it is a copied design.

indicators.note: the 51 has got into the area word, so its letters sit inside

parts.note: a region is an area
LI is 51 in Roman numerals; 's is 'has'

explanation.surface: Faith that Area 51, the secret US base, has been infiltrated — a conspiracy theorist's creed.
explanation.definitionFit: A religion is a system of faith, so it is a belief.

indicators.note: 'no hotel' says the hotel letter is absent from the squat word

parts.note: squat means short and stocky
Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A ranking of places to stay: the squat is not a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: To rank things is to sort them into order; both are verbs of classifying.

clue.text: Prey led astray bears feed on often

indicators.note: the shuffled letters carry the feeding word within them
letters gone astray have wandered out of order

parts.note: to feed is to eat

explanation.surface: Prey led off course by bears is something they feed on often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' looks like the animals, but is the verb 'carries', holding the eating word inside the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something repeatedly means doing it again and again, that is, often.

clue.text: Vocal criticism, for instance, over holding one dance

parts.note: a boo is criticism shouted aloud

indicators.note: the turned example letters hold the one inside them
in a down clue 'over' turns the example abbreviation upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: e.g. is short for 'for example', i.e. for instance
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Booing a performer, for instance, over a single dance number.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vocal' suggests singing, but here it just means shouted criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: The boogie is a lively style of dancing to rock or pop music.

clue.text: 50-year-old record that is sealing mother with her ruin?

indicators.note: the 'that is' letters close around the mother and her ruin, sealing them in

parts.note: Ma is a familiar word for mother
gin is popularly called 'mother's ruin'

explanation.surface: An old record seals away a mother and the thing that ruined her.
explanation.walkthrough: John Lennon's 'Imagine' came out in 1971, fifty years before this 2021 puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lennon's song was released half a century earlier, so it is a fifty-year-old recording.

clue.text: Traditional number of vegetables nearly always consumed by the French

parts.note: greens are leafy green vegetables

indicators.note: the French article eats up the shortened always word, which sits within it

parts.note: les is French for 'the' (plural)

indicators.note: nearly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: A set number of vegetables is always eaten by the French, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is a piece of music, not a count; the shortened always word sits inside the French article after its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Greensleeves is an English folk tune dating from Tudor times, a traditional piece of music.

clue.text: Parts of limbs left in dens

indicators.note: the left letter is placed in the dens word

parts.note: caves are animals' dens

explanation.surface: Limbs left lying in animals' dens, the remains of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts of limbs' looks like bones left in a lair; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The calf is the fleshy back part of the lower leg, so calves are parts of limbs.

definitions.meaning: a shower of frozen pellets of ice

explanation.surface: Greeting someone with a bracing cold shower.
explanation.definitionFit: Hail means to greet, and as a noun it is precipitation falling as ice pellets.

indicators.note: to don is to put on, so the discount word wears the 'for' word inside

parts.note: a rebate is a discount
pro is Latin for 'for', as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: A discount offered to university dons is denounced as wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like university teachers but is the verb 'puts on'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled person, and as an adjective it means morally depraved, i.e. wicked.

parts.note: the fantastic servant is the genie; his home is opened by rubbing it, and 1 across is a rubbing

explanation.surface: A cryptic reference back to 1 across: what home does rubbing open?
explanation.walkthrough: In the tale, rubbing the lamp summons the genie who lives in it; 1 across, BRASS RUBBING, supplies the rubbing.
explanation.definitionFit: The genie of the fairy tale dwells in a magic oil lamp that is rubbed to release him.

indicators.note: pruning cuts something back, so the desire word loses its last letter

parts.note: love is desire
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A gardener's longing to prune a full-grown plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovage is a tall herb of the parsley family, used in cooking — a plant.

indicators.note: letters that are organised are put into a new order

parts.note: a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: A VIP has arranged a shelter for a cat, continued in the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A pavilion is a light building or tent giving shelter, such as at a sports ground.

clue.text: Supervisory staff lofty around group's leader

parts.note: to man something is to staff it

indicators.note: the lofty word goes around the group's leader

parts.note: aerial means high up, lofty

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Supervisors staff a high-up office around the group's boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes G from 'group's', which 'around' places inside AERIAL after its first A.
explanation.definitionFit: Managerial describes the work of managers, who supervise others.

clue.text: … old cat dies after shuffling out of place

indicators.note: once the letters are shuffled they make a new word

explanation.surface: Continuing 13: the old cat dies after being moved about.
explanation.definitionFit: A dislocated joint has been displaced, knocked out of its proper position.

clue.text: We're told, ring for cosmetic treatment

indicators.note: something we are told is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to peal is to ring, as bells do

explanation.surface: We're told that a ring is a beauty treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemical peel removes the outer skin layer of the face as a beauty procedure.

indicators.note: vandalised letters are wrecked and rearranged
unopened means the word loses its first letter, its opening

explanation.surface: A receptacle left unopened by a miscreant who vandalised it.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a round container, a receptacle for tea, film or gas.

indicators.note: back means the hidden letters are read in reverse
the word orthopaedic cushions, or holds, the letters within it

explanation.surface: A fancy orthopaedic cushion for the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cushions' holds AEDI inside 'orthopaedic'; 'back' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a notion or thought, the same as an idea.

indicators.note: the two words tackle, or grip, the letters inside them

explanation.surface: A sportsperson out riding meets an eleven making terrifying tackles.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer is a horse or rider competing in equestrian eventing.

clue.text: Alleviating hurt via tea and pill

indicators.note: hurt letters are damaged and rearranged

explanation.surface: Relieving pain by means of tea and a pill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' simply links the fodder; the anagram uses the letters of VIA TEA PILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Palliative care alleviates symptoms without curing, so palliative means easing or relieving.

indicators.note: in a down clue the function word goes below the spirit word

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous spirit
to act is to function

explanation.surface: A function under the influence of spirits has a strong effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests drink but is a small demon.
explanation.definitionFit: Impact is a forceful influence or marked effect.

clue.text: Article in silence split by good shooter

indicators.note: the article goes in the silence word

parts.note: mum means silence, as in 'mum's the word'

indicators.note: the article is split apart by the good letter

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article about silence being broken by a skilled marksman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooter' is slang for a gun, not a person who shoots.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnum is a powerful revolver, so a shooter in the slang sense of a gun.

parts.note: to see is to consider or judge
sawed means cut with a saw

explanation.surface: A judge pruned a rose bush, which then toppled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like the flower but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that seesawed moved up and down alternately, rising then falling.

parts.note: to tip something is to upset it

indicators.note: occasionally means only some letters are taken, every other one

explanation.surface: A drink knocked over and spilt now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipple is an alcoholic drink, especially one habitually taken.

indicators.note: the northerner's word comes first in the answer, before the other pronoun

parts.note: 'un is northern English dialect for 'one', a pronoun
it is a pronoun

explanation.surface: A group supplying grammar lessons on pronouns, with a northerner going first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronouns' covers both: 'UN (as in 'a good 'un') from northern England dialect, and IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a group of people or things forming a whole, such as a military unit.

indicators.note: for the ear means as heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a tension is a strain; said aloud, 'a tension' gives the answer

explanation.surface: A medical hearing test: a strain on the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone covers both words: 'a tension' run together.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a hearing is to pay attention to what they say.

clue.text: Food wagon overlooking near side of road

indicators.note: overlooking means missing out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a truck is a wagon

indicators.note: the near side of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A food wagon parked overlooking the near side of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: TUCK is British school slang for snacks and sweets.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuck is informal British word for food, especially snacks eaten by schoolchildren.

clue.text: Soldier from capital turned on mean country, changing sides

indicators.note: the turned capital is placed on, i.e. after, the mean word

parts.note: par is the mean or average

indicators.note: turned means the capital is read backwards

parts.note: Lima is the capital of Peru

indicators.note: changing sides swaps left for right, so the letter for left becomes the letter for right

parts.note: Italy is a European country

explanation.surface: A soldier from the capital turned on a mean country, then defected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives AMIL; 'changing sides' turns ITALY into ITARY (L, left, becomes R, right).
explanation.definitionFit: A paramilitary is a member of an irregular force organised like an army, a kind of soldier.
